comment.body:
Hello. 

Every use case in this thread already has a cheaper primitive. Per-endpoint auth is detectable with HEAD + status, mime/size with a probe upload, the operator pubkey is solvable with a domain→pubkey mapping along the lines of NIP-05, and policy/contact info lives just fine on the HTML homepage the server is already serving anyway. 

As for discovery, that's an O(N) problem and it's better solved by an external directory than by N unverifiable self-descriptions. The BUD doesn't close any real gap, in fact, it duplicates channels that already exist.

The cost, in my opinion, is permanent. Once the endpoint is part of the spec, every conforming client inherits questions that didn't exist before. For examble fetch ordering relative to the first upload, cache TTL, behavior on 4xx/5xx/timeout, etc. These specs don't get un-merged, and the surface that grows on top of them constrains every subsequent BUD.

As for precedents (NIP-11 and NUT-06) both ended up exactly where @hzrd149 already pointed out. And someone in this thread has already said they want to extend the document with non-standard fields 🤣. Add to that the impersonation issue @fiatjaf raised (a self-declared name is strictly weaker than the domain Blossom already inherits for free), and the balance doesn't add up. My opinion, **close it.**

issue.title: Add Blossom server compliance test suite
issue.body:
## Summary

- Adds a comprehensive compliance test suite covering **BUD-00 through BUD-12**, validating Blossom server implementations against the BUD specifications
- Each BUD has its own test module (`bud-XX.test.ts`) with both mandatory and optional behavior checks
- Includes an HTML + JSON report generator (`report.ts`) with per-server and per-BUD breakdowns

## What's included

**Test modules** (`bud-00.test.ts` – `bud-12.test.ts`):
- BUD-00: Server reachability
- BUD-01: Server requirements (CORS, error responses, blob retrieval, HEAD, range requests)
- BUD-02: Blob upload (PUT /upload, descriptors, X-SHA-256, duplicate handling)
- BUD-03: Skipped (client-side only, no server endpoints)
- BUD-04: Blob mirror (PUT /mirror, descriptor validation, error cases)
- BUD-05: Blob delete (DELETE /<sha256>, authorization)
- BUD-06: Blob upload (media) (PUT /media)
- BUD-07: Blob list (GET /list/<pubkey>)
- BUD-08: Blob TTL (upload with expiry)
- BUD-09: Blob report (PUT /report with kind:1984 events)
- BUD-10: Skipped (client-side only)
- BUD-11: Auth tokens (kind:24242, header validation)
- BUD-12: Identical blob deduplication

**Helpers** (`helpers/`):
- `http.ts` — HTTP request wrapper with auto-retry on 401 (detects auth-required servers)
- `nostr.ts` — Key pair generation, kind:24242 auth event building, base64url encoding
- `crypto.ts` — SHA-256 hashing, random bytes/blobs
- `assert.ts` — Assertion framework with pass/fail/warn/skip states
- `cleanup.ts` — Tracks and deletes uploaded blobs after each test run
- `test-blob.ts` — Generates unique PNG test images with Blossom branding
- `config.ts` — Server URL configuration via `BLOSSOM_SERVER_URL` env var

**Report generator** (`report.ts`):
- Runs all BUD tests against one or multiple servers
- Outputs `results.json` and styled `index.html` with pass/fail/warn breakdowns

## Usage

```bash
cd compliance-test
bun install

# Test a single server
BLOSSOM_SERVER_URL=https://your-server.com bun run report.ts

# Or import individual test modules
BLOSSOM_SERVER_URL=https://your-server.com bun test
```

issue.title: Proposal: Blob Ownership
issue.body:
### Summary

This PR introduces **Blob Ownership**, an ownership model for blobs where:
- Multiple pubkeys can be owners of a single blob
- Anyone can become an owner by claiming ownership
- Blobs may be deleted when no owners remain

### Motivation

**Immutable uploads**: Alice uploads a blob and designates Bob as the sole owner. Alice cannot delete it alone, ensuring the blob persists even if the uploader changes their mind.

### [BUD here](https://nostrhub.io/naddr1qvzqqqrcvypzpv3tq6c9rl2jx2tx4y6y5c6dj4krmse60a0vmjkea5gam3qjpfljqythwumn8ghj7un9d3shjtnrv9kk2mr4wvhxzursqqfxyaty943xcmmz94hhwmn9wfeks6ts5v4rhj)

issue.title: /media endpoint should allow more flexibility.
issue.body: While I am happy to see there is a way to optimize the media, there is no provision for any sort of HLS/DASH transcoding with VBR (variable bitrate) or any other optimizations. If we were to allow for YT like experience, and potentially reusage of the transcoding burden, the current scheme will prevent any improvements in this space, and will limit any video content to a short clip. There is also a question of uploads that would exceed server limitations, and would benefit from usage of TUS (or similar standard) to break them down into smaller chunks to allow resume or parallel uploading.

comment.body:
I understand your intention. However, from a user perspective I think the media hosting server makes the most sense for this role, so I think it was the right call to add this as an optional feature that Blossom servers may or may not do. As a new user, you already have to somewhat understand what relays and file/media servers are, which is much more complex than having one server for all of it (regardless of it being centralized or federated or p2p). Adding additional (probably authenticated) services on top adds friction both in hosting and using apps that deal with images. It also adds additional server connections and round trips, both HTTP and WebSockets.

That said, I do see the need for separate services when it comes to transcoding video. At least much more so than with photos. My hunch for moving forward with the existing BUD would be that if there's any kind of media optimization being done, then the endpoints, rules, and settings for photos and videos should likely not be the same.

FWIW, during testing of my PWA's photo uploads over the last couple of days, the processing time especially on my phone is basically the last remaining pain point when using the photo upload feature. (Since `createImageBitmap` is kind of flaky in Chromium on Android, my app is already falling back to stepped downscaling via canvas, and it's already using `OffscreenCanvas` in a worker. So there's not much more I can do client-side to improve the situation.)

comment.body:
Similarly, for photo uploads, it would be very useful to not only have the server decide how to optimize the image, because it also depends on the use case, which only the client can know.

For example, in my app I'm creating both full-size photos and thumbnails, and I'm also specifying a different JPEG quality between them. With the current spec, I could move the full-size processing to the media endpoint and hope that the servers I don't control optimize in a way that it looks good in my app and still loads reasonably fast on mobile connections. However, I can't move processing of thumbnails at all.
